Resuming: inspecting current native state of 6:2 and 6:15 before placing the stamp.Round trip complete, with one honest limit on the final export step.

**Done in Figma (file 1UGF8VTtWSz0D3pjGvOWwf)**
- New frame **Garden-agent revision** is node 6:2, cloned from 5:2 and placed to its right. Source frames 3:2 and 5:2 are unchanged.
- Event text in the new frame (node 6:7) reads exactly `EDITED · 10 AM` / `The community garden`, re-read after every write.
- Small improvements: 24px corner radius, a short terracotta accent rule above the event details, a soft shadow on the pot.
- garden-stamp.svg uploaded via upload_assets and imported as editable vectors (node 6:15), then moved into 6:2 as an absolute badge in the bottom-right corner, 56px from the edges and 37px below the copy column. It doesn't overlap the event text or illustration.
- Write access was proven by real clone, edit and upload calls even though whoami reports a View seat.

**Local files written**
- `figma-output.png` (960x720, MCP render of 6:2, inspected visually: everything reads cleanly).
- `roundtrip.json` with file/node IDs, preserved text, upload/download paths, hashes and verification results.

**Limit hit**
The Figma MCP call limit on the Starter plan (20 read calls per month) triggered on the download_assets export and a final metadata re-read of 5:2. Both attempts were rejected. figma-output.png is therefore the get_screenshot render fetched just before the limit, not a download_assets export. This is recorded in roundtrip.json. Nothing else was touched: no publishing, sharing, .crux, AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.

{"contents":[{"uri":"file://figma/docs/rate-limits-access.md","mimeType":"text/markdown","text":"# Rate limits & access ## Who can access the MCP server? Access to the Figma MCP server depends on your Figma plan and seat type. Per-minute rate limits apply in addition to daily or monthly tool call limits.
Seat Starter Professional Organization Enterprise
View, Collab Up to 20/month Up to 6/month Up to 6/month Up to 6/month
Dev, Full Up to 200/day
10/min		 Up to 200/day
15/min		 Up to 600/day
20/min
**Note:** Education plans use the same rate limits as Dev and Full seats on the Professional plan: up to 200 tool calls per day, 10 per minute. Rate limits apply to Figma MCP server tools that read data from Figma. Some tools, such as those that write to Figma files, are exempt from the rate limits. Exempt tools include: - `add_code_connect_map` - `create_new_file` - `whoami` Figma reserves the right to change rate limits. ## What if I'm rate-limited? If you're encountering rate limits with the Figma MCP server, you can increase your limits in certain scenarios by upgrading your seat or plan. - If you're on a Starter plan (20 tool calls per month), upgrade to a Pro, Organization, or Enterprise plan. Ensure you have a Full or Dev seat on the new plan. - If you have a View or Collab seat on an Organization or Enterprise plan (6 tool calls per month), upgrade to a Full or Dev seat. - If you have a Full or Dev seat on an Organization plan (200 tool calls per day), upgrade to an Enterprise plan (600 tool calls per day). - If you're on an Education plan (200 tool calls per day), upgrade to an Organization or Enterprise plan for higher limits. Full and Dev seats on Enterprise plans get the least-limited usage, as described in [Who can access the MCP server?](#who-can-access-the-mcp-server) ## Does the Figma MCP server support enterprise-managed authorization? Yes. Currently, enterprise-managed authorization is supported only for Claude via Okta Cross App Access (XAA). Normally, the Figma MCP server requires each user to follow an OAuth login flow to get access. Using Okta XAA, access is brokered by Okta: a member signs in once through Okta, and Claude can then work with the Figma MCP server without asking that member to authorize again. To learn more, see [Set up OIDC for Okta XAA](https://help.figma.com/hc/articles/41992841175959) in Figma's Help Center. ## Which MCP clients are supported? To use the MCP server, you’ll need a code editor or application that supports MCP servers (for example, VS Code, Cursor, or Claude Code). Only clients listed in the [Figma MCP Catalog](https://www.figma.com/mcp-catalog/) are able to connect to the Figma MCP Server. If you’re a developer interested in connecting a new MCP client, you can [join the waitlist](https://form.asana.com/?k=kBG-ejRQTdY8x_H6a4vM3Q&d=10497086658021). ## Why am I getting permission errors? You can only access Figma content that you already have permission to view or edit. If you get an error indicating that resources can’t be accessed: 1. **Check the file link:** Make sure it’s a valid Figma Design, FigJam, or Figma Make file. 2. **Verify your user:** Run the whoami tool to confirm the email used for authentication. It also tells you all the plans the user belongs to and their seat types in these plans. 3. **Confirm permissions:** Ensure the user belongs to the plan to which the file being accessed belongs to as well "}]}
